name: Raider tail crowded - a multi-tile mover blocked by a tile that is not its own anchor
notes: A minimal, deterministic-by-construction replacement for the emergent 'raider crowded by an ally's tail' case speed-parade.map.json used to produce incidentally: that scenario's own job is a speed demonstration, not a regression fixture, and the exact tick its movers happened to crowd each other drifted (twice now) every time a movement-speed pass changed the fixture roster's rates. This fixture instead builds the case directly. The raider (3x1) approaches a hostile due east, purely on-axis (Q15) so east is its only improving direction. A friendly den sits one tile further east than the raider's own next step - its own nearest tile (the raider's own anchor after stepping) is clear ground, but the tile at the *far* end of the raider's post-step footprint is not. The bug this pins: the report used to check only the mover's own anchor tile and, finding it clear, called the block 'edge' - the fallback for 'nothing was wrong with the one tile I looked at' - misreporting a crowded ally as the Grid's own border. footprintBlockerAt (src/grid/occupancy.ts) checks the whole footprint instead.
